newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says killed 23 rebels in clashes.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says killed 23 rebels in clashes.

text.p: Turkish security forces killed 23 rebels in the last two days in southeast Turkey, a statement from the emergency rule governor's office said on Sunday.
The statement said that 16 "terrorists", a term normally used to refer to members of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK), were killed in clashes in Bingol province and seven killed in Tunceli province.
Those killed in Tunceli were said to have belonged to the far-left Turkish Workers and Peasants Liberation Army (TIKKO).

The hardline Maoist group, TIKKO, has been targeting soldiers police and village chiefs in Tunceli since the 1970s, but its attacks have been limited in recent years. TIKKO sometimes stages joint attacks with the PKK separatist rebels.
Five members of the armed Islamist group, Hizbullah, were also arrested in Diyarbakir, the statement said.

Hizbullah is not believed to be connected to the pro-Iranian Lebanese based group of a similar name. It has been accused of killing a number of Kurdish activists in recent years as part of a feud with the PKK.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the 12-year struggle between the Turkish security forces and the PKK, which is fighting for independence or autonomy in Turkey's mainly Kurdish southeast.
